lessons.title: Dedução com must, might e can't
lessons.goal: Dominar a gramática da unidade: Dedução no presente: must be, might / may / could be, can't be.

head: Modal
Grau de certeza
Exemplo
rows: quase certeza de que é verdade
She must be tired. She's been working all day.
He might be Paulo. He's tall and has glasses.
quase certeza de que NÃO é
That can't be his jacket. It's too expensive.

aula.text: Para algo acontecendo agora, use o *continuous*: *He must be working.*

aula.label: Atenção
aula.text: aqui *must* não é obrigação, é dedução. O oposto de *must be* é **can't be**, não *mustn't*.

items: "He mustn't be at home, the lights are off." O certo é **He can't be at home.**
"He maybe is late." O certo é **He may be late** ou **Maybe he is late.** (maybe, uma palavra, vem antes do sujeito)

exercises.prompt: The lights are on. He ___ (be) at home.
exercises.ctx: Paulo walks past Ana's house at night.

exercises.ctx: At a party, Clara sees a woman far away.

exercises.ctx: Clara sees a very skinny man and thinks of Paulo.

He cannot be at home, the lights are off

exercises.ctx: Clara talks about a friend who hasn't arrived.

exercises.ctx: Clara looks at a woman who has just arrived.

exercises.prompt: He ___ (be) a teacher. He's carrying a lot of books. I'm quite sure.
exercises.ctx: Clara sees a man on the bus.

exercises.prompt: Rita ___ (be) in Paris. I saw her at the market this morning.
exercises.ctx: A friend says Rita is on holiday.

exercises.prompt: I don't know where he is. He ___ (be) at the gym or he ___ (be) at home.

exercises.prompt: Look at someone near you. What do you think about him or her? Use must, might or can't.

exercises.note: must = quase certeza; might = possibilidade; can't = quase certeza que não.

aula.text: *look* + adjetivo (*looks tired*). *look like* + substantivo (*looks like a doctor*).

items: "He looks like tired." O certo é **He looks tired.**
